brief: A calendar showing energy levels — mornings are high ground, post-lunch dips are valleys

dominant_strengths: Clear calendar grid scaffolding with consistent typographic hierarchy makes day numbers and scores immediately scannable
Bold gradient bars create a visceral, almost topographic 'energy ridge' metaphor aligned with the brief
Score chips reuse the legend palette, giving day-level summary that ties to the bar visualization
dominant_weaknesses: Each cell shows three nearly identical stacked bars — they don't encode time-of-day peaks/valleys, so the 'morning high, post-lunch dip' narrative is invisible
Color legend promises four states but bars are uniform gradients per cell; semantic mapping between chip color and bar shape is unclear and redundant
Only one cell shows a time axis (6AM/12PM/6PM); without it across cells, the bars read as decorative fills rather than data
fix_priorities: Replace stacked bars with a single sparkline/area curve per day showing AM peak and PM valley to literally execute the brief
Drop redundant duplicate bars; use one bar with hue-shifted segments mapped to legend categories
Add a faint time axis or tick marks behind every cell so the curve is interpretable at a glance
Tone down saturated red/orange that currently reads as alarm rather than 'low energy'
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral punch from neon gradients outpaces behavioral clarity, leaving reflective insight (when am I actually low?) underdelivered.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially — the calendar exists and scores are present, but the bars fail to depict morning peaks vs post-lunch valleys, so the central metaphor is unrealized.
